title: Integrative machine-learning repositioning framework identifies CVL218 against SARS-CoV-2
summary: A framework combining machine learning and statistical analysis over knowledge-graph, literature and transcriptome data screened drug candidates for COVID-19. The PARP1 inhibitor CVL218 inhibited SARS-CoV-2 replication in vitro without obvious cytopathic effect, interacted with the nucleocapsid protein and suppressed LPS-induced inflammatory cytokines.
ai_technology: Machine learning and statistical mining of knowledge-graph, literature and transcriptome data for drug repositioning
organization: Tsinghua University; Jiangsu Provincial Center for Diseases Control and Prevention

evidence.tested: In vitro antiviral, N-protein binding and cytokine assays of the selected compound.
evidence.unknown: The abstract describes the machine learning generically; in vitro only, no clinical efficacy; abstract only; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning and statistics prioritised candidate drugs, including CVL218, from integrated data.
